title: Signal Catalog + Runbook for per-route embeddings & rerank telemetry
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a lightweight, production-safe signal catalog and on-call runbook for per-route embeddings and reranking traffic. The goal is to give SREs, platform engineers, and product owners clear signals to detect quality regressions, cost spikes, and latency SLO violations specific to route configurations (model variant, batching, cache policy). Deliverables: signal catalog, tracing/span conventions, Grafana dashboard templates (per-route), alert rules, sample saved queries for chargeback, and an incident remediation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Signal catalog document published and linked in Console Observability section
Grafana template that can be instantiated per-route with variables (route_id, model_variant)
Tracing spans and tag conventions committed and in runtime instrumentation PR
Alert rules created for: p95 inference latency, rerank cost per request, embedding encode error rate, cache hit rate drop
Runbook with step-by-step remediation and fallback toggles validated in a runbook dry-run
Chargeback query for daily cost per route produces results for top 50 routes
tasks: Define top-level signals and their collection method (metrics vs traces vs logs)
Design per-route dashboard panels and variable schema
Instrument runtime: add route_id, request_id, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit to spans/metrics
Implement cardinality controls: route sampling + aggregations to avoid high metric cardinality
Create Grafana/Tempo dashboards and templated JSON
Author runbook: alerts -> triage -> mitigation -> rollback
Add chargeback SQL (BigQuery) for token/embedding/rerank cost attribution
Create PRD + console feature flag to enable detailed telemetry for beta customers
success_metrics: Time to detect major rerank quality regression reduced to <= 5 minutes after deployment
False positive alert rate for per-route rerank alerts < 10% after tuning
Top-10 high-cost routes identified and actionable recommendations generated within 2 weeks
Median time-to-mitigation during incidents < 20 minutes when runbook followed
Sampling/tracing overhead on p95 latency < +5ms for enabled routes
implementation_notes: Prefer metrics (aggregated counters/histograms) where possible; reserve traces for tail analysis and root cause
Use lightweight span tags: route_id, model_variant, scorer_step (encode, index_search, reranker), batch_count
Add kv_cache metrics: hits, misses, eviction_rate per route to tie cache behavior to latency/cost
Cardinality control: only attach full route metadata when route is in debug mode or sampled (1-5%)
Chargeback: compute cost tokens -> GPU-second mapping using runtime profiling table; attribute by route via request tags
Tracing retention: keep full traces for 7 days for sampled traffic; use indexed trace IDs in logs for longer compliance needs
Fallback actions: warm cache, switch to cheaper model_variant, degrade to embedding-only reranking, or route to degraded SLA tier
tradeoffs_and_risks: High-cardinality labels (route + customer + model_variant) will increase metric cardinality and storage costs — mitigate with sampling and aggregation buckets
Enabling full tracing increases p95 latency slightly; default to sampling and opt-in detailed traces for high-value customers
Chargeback accuracy is approximated from profiling; exact per-request GPU usage is noisy, document estimation error bounds
Runbook recommended mitigations might affect customer experience (fallback to cheaper models) — require PM approval for auto-remediation rules
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Deploy signal collection to internal routes only; validate dashboards and runbook with SREs (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta customers): Enable per-route telemetry for opt-in customers and product partners; collect feedback (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Turn on default aggregated route metrics for all customers; keep tracing sampling at 1% unless route flagged
Phase 4 (GA): Publish templated dashboards in Console and add pre-built alerts; enable chargeback queries in billing report
runbook: Alert: p95_inference_latency(route) > SLO_threshold for 5 minutes -> Acknowledge in PagerDuty
Step 1: Check per-route Grafana panel: baseline p50/p95, batch sizes, kv_cache_hit -> identify spike dimension
Step 2: Inspect sampled traces for route_id within last 10m in Tempo; look for slow spans: encode vs index_search vs reranker
Step 3: If kv_cache_hit rate dropped > 30%: trigger cache-warm job for affected route, increase cache TTL if safe
Step 4: If reranker span is hot: consider switching to cheaper model_variant (feature flag) or reduce rerank_k for short window
Step 5: If cost-per-request unexpectedly high: throttle low-priority routes via rate-limiter and open chargeback investigation
Step 6: Post-incident: run retro and add missing signals to catalog if any blind spots found
open_questions: What is acceptable sampling rate for traces that balances root-cause fidelity vs overhead? (engineering proposal: 1%)
Should we expose per-customer cost attribution in Console or limit to admins/billing exports?
How to reconcile approximate cost model with enterprise invoicing requirements?
What guardrails are required before enabling auto-remediation (e.g., switching model_variant) on production routes?
